title: Web Application Tracer Project Knowledge Base
description: Machine-readable software blueprint and charter for the Web Application Tracer (web_tracer): a cross-layer tracer that records one user action and reconstructs it as an interactive execution tree spanning the browser, HTTP transport, backend service, database and external calls.

project_metadata.name: Web Application Tracer (web_tracer)
project_metadata.description: Cross-layer web application tracer that records a single user action and rebuilds it as an interactive execution tree across the browser, HTTP, backend, database and external-service layers.
project_metadata.purpose: Let non-specialist users and developers see exactly which functions, endpoints and database calls one click triggers, across every software layer, to support troubleshooting, onboarding and change-impact analysis.
project_metadata.status: Phase 4 complete (T34-T40, 2026-10-02): correlation engine (trace_id + URL/time fallback), execution tree, correlation report and a dashboard (served at GET /) with the tree tab and a cross-layer span inspector. Phase 5 (Python static analysis) is next.

engine/java/otlp_decode.py (T29) - decode OTLP/HTTP protobuf|json ExportTraceServiceRequest into SpanEvents; ProtobufUnavailable downgrade when protobuf missing; _classify maps OTel span -> layer/event_type/kind; _map_otel_span validates each span

engine/correlation/engine.py (T34) - CorrelationEngine: clock normalisation onto the browser base clock (per-collector median clock_offset_ms, correction recorded in clock.offset_ms), primary trace_id join at confidence 1.0, fallback dispatch, and parent_overrides stitching the Java handler under the browser request span

data_flows: Browser events (click/submit/fetch) -> initiator mapping -> HTTP spans carrying traceparent
HTTP request -> backend OpenTelemetry span (Python, @traced decorator, Q1) -> downstream DB / external spans
Browser spans + backend spans -> correlation engine (traceparent match) -> UnifiedGraph {nodes, edges, entry_points, hotspots, stats}
UnifiedGraph -> interactive dashboard tree on :8100 (expand/collapse, jump to source line)
Static Python analysis (tree-sitter-python) -> python_call_graph.json -> merged into UnifiedGraph as static_call edges
integration_points: Target application Case A: dcc pipeline UI served by dcc/serve.py (Python 3.13, port 5000); web_tracer drives a pipeline run and traces it cross-layer
OpenTelemetry OTLP receiver (Phase 0/3) - backend spans arrive over OTLP
Playwright (Phase 2) - browser runtime capture; Selenium BiDi / CDP adapters deferred to Phase 8
Shared common/universal_ui_design.css + .js - base UI design system (5 themes, shell layout, toast/modal/file/table utils)
W3C traceparent - the correlation key joining browser and backend traces

core_entities: Trace - one complete cross-layer recording of a single user action, rooted at the browser action
Span - a timed unit of work (DOM handler, HTTP call, backend function, DB query) with trace_id/span_id/parent
SpanEvent - a structured point-in-time event carried by a span (the canonical span payload, T03)
ExecutionTree - the per-layer tree of spans before correlation
UnifiedGraph - merged cross-layer graph {nodes, edges, entry_points, hotspots, stats} (T04)
Node - a graph vertex: kind page/component/function/endpoint; layer browser/http/python/db/external; carries file_path + start_line
Endpoint - an HTTP route recorded on a node (node.endpoints[]) and matched browser<->backend
Traceparent - W3C propagation header '00-<trace_id>-<span_id>-01' that joins the layers
UserAction - the recorded trigger (e.g. click:#toolbarRunBtn) that seeds the trace root
Hotspot - a node flagged as costly or frequently on the critical path, surfaced in stats
relationships: event_bind - DOM element bound to a JS handler (browser layer)
static_call - determinable function/method call resolved by static analysis
dynamic_call - call resolved only at runtime (e.g. dispatch by name)
http_call - browser fetch/XHR to a backend endpoint (becomes node.endpoints[])
initiator - an HTTP request linked to its response span
correlation - the edge that joins a browser trace to its backend trace via traceparent
terminology: UnifiedGraph - the merged cross-layer execution graph (browser + HTTP + backend + DB + external)
traceparent - W3C distributed-tracing header used as the correlation key across layers
SpanEvent - the canonical span payload schema frozen in T03
hotspot - a node on the critical path or with high cost, highlighted in the dashboard
entry point - the browser action or endpoint that roots a trace or subgraph
Correlation Engine - the component that stitches browser and backend spans into one tree
Case A - cross-layer target: dcc pipeline UI served on :5000 (Correlation Engine active)
Case B - standalone interactive HTML opened via file:// (browser-only; Correlation Engine idle)

key_schemas: schema/span_schema.json (T03, planned) - SpanEvent schema; must accept both proposal examples and the three §8.3 examples; rejects illegal spans
schema/execution_tree_schema.json (T04, planned) - per-layer execution-tree schema; the §8.3.2 example must validate
schema/unified_graph_schema.json (T04, planned) - merged graph schema {nodes, edges, entry_points, hotspots, stats}; the §8.3.3 example must validate
schema/validate.py (T03/T04, planned) - validator invoked before any artefact is written

workflows.name: Phase 0 Spike - cross-layer trace of a dcc pipeline run (Case A)
phases: Drive dcc/serve.py on :5000 and trigger a pipeline run from the dashboard
Capture browser spans + backend OpenTelemetry spans across the serve.py -> dcc_engine_pipeline.py subprocess boundary
Verify traceparent is propagated across the subprocess boundary; otherwise the tree splits (key Phase 0 gate)

workflows.name: Record a user action (Phase 2)
workflows.description: Browser captures DOM events, maps HTTP initiators to spans, and the user action becomes the trace root; also starts the OTLP receiver

workflows.name: Correlate and build the tree (Phase 3/4)
workflows.description: Correlation Engine matches browser and backend spans by traceparent and prints/returns the UnifiedGraph

workflows.name: Serve the dashboard (Phase 1)
workflows.description: Start the web server on :8100 and open the interactive execution-tree dashboard

workflows.name: Static analysis (Phase 5)
workflows.description: tree-sitter-python extracts python_call_graph.json and merges static_call edges into the UnifiedGraph

workflows.name: Correlate a run and render the execution tree (Phase 4)
workflows.description: Loads browser_trace.json + java_trace.json for the run, joins request spans to server handlers by trace_id (1.0) then by URL + +/-200 ms window (<=0.8), writes correlation_report.json and execution_tree.json into output/runs/<run_id>, and the dashboard renders the tree from GET /execution_tree/{run_id}

data_flows.name: Cross-layer trace assembly
data_flows.source: A single user action in the browser (e.g. click:#toolbarRunBtn on the dcc pipeline dashboard)
transformations: BrowserTracer records DOM events and maps HTTP initiators to spans carrying traceparent
Backend OpenTelemetry SDK emits spans for the Python handler (@traced) and downstream DB/external calls
traceparent is propagated across the serve.py -> dcc_engine_pipeline.py subprocess boundary
Correlation Engine matches browser and backend spans by traceparent
UnifiedGraph is built and rendered as an interactive tree in the dashboard
data_flows.destination: output/ UnifiedGraph artefacts + interactive dashboard on :8100

data_flows.name: Static augmentation
data_flows.source: Project source tree (Python, Case A target dcc)
transformations: Edges typed static_call / dynamic_call; endpoints recorded on nodes

data_flows.name: Correlation and execution tree (Phase 4)
transformations: clock normalisation onto the browser base clock
fallback method+path + +/-200 ms window join - 0.8 unique / 0.6 ambiguous / 0.4 path-only
unmatched requests classified with one of six reasons (never silently dropped)
tree built from parent_span_id, synthetic root for orphans, cycle guard
start_offset_ms / self_time_ms / stats computed and schema-validated
data_flows.destination: output/runs/<run_id>/correlation_report.json + execution_tree.json, rendered by the dashboard tree tab and Span inspector

data_quality_checks: Span schema validation (T03) - illegal spans rejected before write
UnifiedGraph / ExecutionTree schema validation (T04) - §8.3.2/§8.3.3 examples must pass
Contract checker (T06) - injected mismatched endpoint fails CI and names the URL
Undefined-function static check (T07) - scans ui/ for calls with no definition; no false positives on static_dashboard.html
Capability probe (T01) - a missing required dependency makes the UI show FATAL, never a bare crash

layers: L1: Project structure validation - the ten required folders exist (T00 established)
L2: Environment probe - Python version + conda env + key packages (engine.capability, T01)
L3: Output-path validation - output/ is writable (engine.paths, T02)
L4: User-input readability - target app path accessible (Phase 0 intake, §12.2)
L5: Dependency probe - per-package availability report (engine.capability, T01)
L6: Readiness override - --skip-readiness CLI bypass (planned, T01)
error_codes: FATAL (capability) - a required dependency is missing; UI shows a red banner
PathEscapeError - a resolved path leaves the allowed root
Contract drift - front end calls a URL the backend does not expose (T06)

external_services: dcc pipeline UI (Case A target) served by dcc/serve.py on :5000 (Python 3.13 conda env 'dcc')
OpenTelemetry OTLP collector/receiver - backend span ingestion (Phase 0/3)

Java/Spring (optional template only, P8) - non-dcc targets; Spring AOP strategy kept as a template, off by default
infrastructure: Python 3.13 (conda env 'web_tracer' created 2026-10-01; required deps: networkx, jsonschema)
Native Linux (current workstation); WSL Ubuntu / Docker Desktop / EKS deferred to later phases
Service port :8100 for the web_tracer dashboard; :5000 for the Case A dcc target
